title: Power is given and taken. It was never yours to keep.
subtitle: A prayer to the Owner of all sovereignty
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say this while praising and trusting his Lord. Ibn Kathir says it encourages {reward}gratitude for the favors granted to him and his community{/reward}, and refutes those who thought they could decide for Allah who deserves His message.
now: You got the promotion. Or the title went to someone else. {idea}Either way, it passed through His hand first.{/idea} That makes the win humble and the loss bearable.
old: My position is something I built and own.
new: Every bit of power or honor I hold is on loan from the Owner.
try: Thank Allah today for one position you hold: parent, manager, elder sibling.

title: Night into day, living from dead. Turning is His habit.
subtitle: The One who turns things around, every day

row.title: it will always be this way

then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah lengthens one and shortens the other through the seasons. He brings {idea}the plant from the seed and the seed from the plant, the faithful from the disbeliever{/idea}, and provides for whom He wills out of wisdom and justice.
now: Winter evenings swallow the afternoon, then summer gives it back. The son who gave up praying starts again. {reward}The account that was empty fills.{/reward} {idea}Nothing you see stays fixed in His hands.{/idea}
old: My situation is stuck, and nothing will change.
new: The One who turns night into day turns situations too.
try: Watch one sunrise or sunset this week and ask Allah to turn one hard thing.

title: Whose side are you on when it counts?
subtitle: Loyalty, and the warning that Allah sees it
then: In Madinah, the young Muslim community faced pressure from many sides. Ibn Kathir explains the verse forbids {trap}taking the enemies of faith as close supporters instead of the believers{/trap}, with an exception for someone who fears for their safety. {idea}Allah warns of Himself, and to Him is the return.{/idea}
now: Your friends mock a fellow Muslim in the group chat, and laughing along keeps you in the circle. {idea}The question is quiet: where does your heart sit when it costs something?{/idea}
old: I go along with whoever keeps me comfortable.
new: My deepest loyalty belongs to Allah, and He knows where my heart leans.
try: Next time someone is mocked for their faith around you, say one kind word for them.

title: Hidden or shown, your heart is known.
subtitle: What you hold inside is not private from Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah's knowledge covers all secret and apparent matters, {idea}not even the weight of an atom escapes Him{/idea}. The verse alerts people to fear Him enough to avoid what He dislikes, since He knows all and is able over all.
now: You smile at your in-law while holding a grudge. You give in the masjid while hoping someone notices. {idea}What you carry inside is as visible to Him as your face.{/idea}
old: As long as I act right, what I feel inside is my business.
new: My heart is open to Allah, so I work on it as much as my actions.
try: Before one good deed today, pause and fix your intention for Allah alone.

title: He warns you because He is kind.
subtitle: Every deed waiting, and a warning that is mercy
then: Ibn Kathir explains every soul will find its good and evil brought before it. Seeing the good brings joy; seeing the evil, one wishes for a great distance from it. Then comes hope: {reward}Al-Hasan Al-Basri said Allah is so kind that He warns them against Himself.{/reward}
now: A good doctor tells you your blood test is bad before it is too late. {reward}That warning is the kindest thing she could do.{/reward} {idea}You still have time to put distance between you and what you regret.{/idea}
old: Warnings about the Day just make me anxious.
new: The warning is mercy, given while I can still change things.
try: Pick one habit you would want far from you on that Day, and take a step away from it.

title: Love Allah? Follow the Prophet, and Allah will love you.
subtitle: The test of a claim to love
then: Ibn Kathir says Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others among the early Muslims explained that {idea}some people claimed to love Allah, so Allah tested them with this verse{/idea}. Ibn Kathir adds that {reward}what they earn is greater than what they sought: Allah's love for them.{/reward}
now: You post a beautiful quote about loving Allah. Then the day goes by without one sunnah. {idea}Love shows in what you copy.{/idea} A smile, a dua before eating, a gentle word.
old: I love Allah in my heart, and that is enough.
new: Love for Allah shows in following His Messenger, and it is answered with His love.
try: Pick one small sunnah you do not do yet and do it today.

title: Obey Allah and the Messenger. That is the whole instruction.
subtitle: A simple command and what turning away means
then: Right after the test of love, the command is put plainly. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}defying the Messenger's way while claiming to love Allah{/trap} is not accepted, and that Allah does not like those who turn away.
now: You know the instruction. The excuse forms quickly: not now, too busy, the situation is different. {idea}The verse is short because the thing is simple.{/idea}
old: I will obey once life is less complicated.
new: Obedience is the simple proof of love, today, in small steps.
try: Do one thing today you know Allah asked of you that you have been delaying.

title: Allah chose Adam, Nuh, and two families.
subtitle: The chosen ones, and the family this surah is named after
then: This opens the part of the surah linked by Maududi to the delegation from Najran. Ibn Kathir explains Allah honored Adam, made Nuh the first messenger, who {idea}called his people day and night for a very long time{/idea}, and chose the families of Ibrahim and Imran, the father of Maryam.
now: You wonder if your life matters in the big story. The chosen ones were not chosen for comfort. {idea}They were chosen to carry something.{/idea} Your own small trust, a child, a parent, a job done well, is part of that line.
old: Being chosen by Allah means things will be easy.
new: Being chosen is a trust to carry, and every believer carries some of it.
try: Read or listen to the story of Nuh in the Quran this week.

title: One family line, passing faith down.
subtitle: Descendants, some from others
then: The chosen families were {idea}descendants, one from the other{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes that Isa came from the offspring of Ibrahim. Allah, All-Hearing and All-Knowing, knew who would carry the trust in each generation.
now: Your kid watches you pray, or watches you skip it. Your niece hears how you talk about your parents. {reward}Faith runs down family lines through small, daily things.{/reward}
old: What I pass on to my kids is mostly money and opportunities.
new: The most lasting thing I pass on is my faith, shown more than said.
try: Let a child in your family see you make dua today, and tell them what you asked for.

title: She gave her unborn child to Allah.
subtitle: A mother's vow before she knew who she carried
then: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn Ishaq that she could not have children, and {idea}seeing a bird feed its chick, she prayed for a child{/idea}. When she knew she was pregnant, she vowed the child to the worship and service of the masjid in Jerusalem.
now: You hold the ultrasound photo, or the baby is asleep on your chest. {reward}The first prayer you make over them shapes what you want for them.{/reward} Success, yes. But also: Allah, let them be Yours.
old: My children are mine to plan for.
new: My children are a trust I can offer back to Allah.
try: Make one dua tonight for a child in your life to be close to Allah.

title: She expected a son. Allah knew better.
subtitle: The birth of Maryam and a mother's protection
then: She had expected a male for service in the masjid. Yet {idea}Allah knew better what she bore.{/idea} She named her Maryam and sought refuge for her and her offspring from Shaytan. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith that {reward}Maryam and her son were not touched by Shaytan at birth.{/reward}
now: The plan did not go your way: a different child, a different job, a different city. {idea}Allah knew better what you were given.{/idea} The mother of Maryam did not argue. She protected what she got.
old: This is not what I asked for, so it is a setback.
new: Allah knows better what He gave me, so I care for it and seek His protection.
try: Say a dua of protection over someone you love today, by name.

title: Where is this from? From Allah.
subtitle: Maryam's provision and Zakariyya's question
then: Allah accepted Maryam and made her grow well, placing her with Zakariyya so she could learn from him. Many early scholars said {reward}he found summer fruit with her in winter and winter fruit in summer.{/reward} Her answer was simple: it is from Allah.
now: A refund arrives the week rent is due. A neighbor drops off food when the fridge is empty. {idea}You ask: where did that come from?{/idea} Maryam already gave the answer.
old: Everything I have comes from my own hard work.
new: My effort matters, but every provision is from Allah.
try: When something good arrives today, say out loud: this is from Allah.
